headline: Fresh US-Iran strikes over the Strait of Hormuz send oil up ~4% and KSE-100 down 1.27% on its ugliest breadth in weeks (13 up, 87 down) — refiners are the lone bright spot on a same-day $6bn upgrade policy.
summary: The US and Iran traded fresh strikes over the weekend, Iran says the Strait of Hormuz is closed (US Central Command disputes that), and oil jumped hard in response — Brent to $78.95 (+3.87% on the day), WTI to $74.14 (+3.82%). Since more than 80% of Pakistan's crude imports transit that strait, the reaction on PSX was immediate and broad: KSE-100 closed at 179,927.04, down 2,314.73 points (-1.27%), with a very weak 13 stocks rising against 87 falling. The desk's macro read has flipped from neutral to risk-off on the back of this, and the one pocket of real strength was refineries (ATRL, NRL, PRL) after the government unveiled a plan to fast-track $6bn of refinery upgrades — everything else oil- and import-cost-sensitive (cement, autos, banks, fertilizer, even E&P, which should theoretically benefit from pricier crude) sold off together in the risk-off sweep. For now the desk is leaning toward quality and defensives and staying patient about chasing names into a headline-driven tape.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: SBP's 11.5% policy rate (next MPC decision Jul 27) keeps net interest margins wide — the classic risk-off carry trade — even though the whole sector traded red today (UBL -1.58%, HBL -0.91%, MCB -1.16%) in the broad selloff.

sectors.name: Fertilizer
sectors.why: Low direct oil-import exposure and defensive domestic demand — FFC (beta 0.28) and ENGROH (beta 0.05) barely move with the index, exactly the ballast the desk wants while Hormuz headlines whip the tape around.

sectors.name: Refineries
sectors.why: A fresh government plan to fast-track $6bn of refinery upgrades made ATRL (+1.93%), NRL (+2.05%) and PRL (+1.57%) today's rare green names, but near-term margins stay exposed to volatile, weekly-repriced crude costs if the Hormuz standoff worsens — a genuine two-sided call.

sectors.name: E&P
sectors.why: Higher realized crude prices should help OGDC, PPL and MARI on paper, but today's tape didn't reward that thesis — all three sold off (PPL -1.75% on the day, -8.01% over 5 sessions) inside the same broad risk-off sweep hitting everything else.

sectors.name: Cement
sectors.why: Energy-intensive and import-cost exposed — DGKC (-3.20%) and MLCF (-3.17%) were among today's five worst-performing KSE-100 names.

sectors.name: Autos
sectors.why: A weaker rupee and pricier imported parts squeeze margins right as June's passenger-car sales fell 12.9% YoY even while FY26 cumulative sales were up 39.4% — the desk's two live technical triggers today (HCAR, GAL) both sit in this macro-flagged sector, a real tension worth watching.

sectors.name: OMCs
sectors.why: PSO's net margin is a wafer-thin 1.4% and prices are repriced weekly now given the volatility — the Jul 11 fuel hike (petrol +Rs13.18, diesel +Rs13.80/litre) passes straight through to consumers rather than boosting OMC profit.

watchlist.angle: Today's most concrete catalyst: government plans to fast-track $6bn of refinery upgrades, with ATRL eligible for a seven-year duty-protection package if it signs an OGRA Upgrade Agreement within 90 days. ATRL was one of only five KSE-100 gainers today (+1.93%), trades above both its 20- and 50-day averages, and the desk's fair-value model reads it 39.7% undervalued (composite fair value Rs1,294 vs a Rs926.51 close). Cheap on paper too — P/E 4.53 is in the bottom third of PSX names.
watchlist.risk: RSI is already at 63.7 and the stock sits within 1% of its 20-day high — much of today's policy optimism may already be priced in, and near-term refiner margins stay hostage to volatile, weekly-repriced crude costs if Hormuz worsens further.

watchlist.angle: Banks are one of the few sectors macro reads as favoured in this risk-off regime, with SBP holding rates at 11.5% (next decision Jul 27). HBL screens attractive: cheap at 6.95x trailing earnings, a 7.65% dividend yield covered by less than half of profit (48% payout), and a forward P/E of 6.46 below trailing, signalling expected earnings growth. The desk's fair-value model reads it roughly fairly priced (+7.3%).
watchlist.risk: It still fell -0.91% today with the rest of the sector in the broad selloff — being macro-favoured doesn't mean immune on a risk-off day — and results aren't due until Aug 11, so there's no near-term catalyst to force a re-rating.

watchlist.angle: Fertilizer is macro's other favoured sector, and FFC tops the desk's predictability rankings across the whole universe (score 67.3). Its proven setup is a 52-week-high breakout (78% historical hit rate, 71% out-of-sample), though it isn't triggering right now — RSI is 47.4 and price sits 4.4% below its 20-day high. Fundamentals lean constructive: forward P/E of 7.02 below trailing 9.39 points to expected earnings growth, and the 6.58% yield is backed by a real 16.5% net margin.
watchlist.risk: No live trigger is firing today, so this is a name to watch rather than an active setup; results are estimated Jul 29 (scraped, unconfirmed date) and a miss would undercut the improving-earnings read.

watchlist.angle: The desk's one live, backtest-proven technical trigger today: a golden cross (50-day SMA crossing above the 200-day), which won 60% of the time across HCAR's own 10-trade history and held up out-of-sample (also 60%). Strategy engine levels: entry 245.56, stop 233.28, target 270.12.
watchlist.risk: This sits squarely in autos, a sector macro is actively flagging to avoid given rupee-driven import costs and softer consumer demand — HCAR's own fundamentals back that caution (P/E 10.84 in the priciest third, thin 2.6% net margin), and the backtest sample is small (only 10 trades). A live trigger firing into a macro headwind and weak fundamentals is a real tension, not a green light.

watchlist.angle: The second live trigger on the board: a trend + momentum combo, medium confidence with a 56.8% historical hit rate over 37 trades (60% out-of-sample). GAL is cheap on paper — 5.19x trailing earnings, forward multiple dropping to 4.68 — and the desk's fair-value model reads it 46.6% undervalued.
watchlist.risk: Same sector tension as HCAR: autos is macro-flagged to avoid, GAL is a small-cap (Rs34.7bn market cap) with thinner liquidity, and today's fuel-price and import-cost backdrop works directly against auto-sector margins and demand.

catalysts.event: HCAR, NESTLE, FFL results (scraped estimates, unconfirmed)
SBP MPC — first FY27 monetary policy decision, watched for a hawkish tilt if the oil shock persists
PBS July 2026 CPI release — first print to capture the Jul 11 fuel hike

risks: Hormuz escalation could deepen further — Iran claims the strait is closed while US CENTCOM disputes it; Pakistan's own Ministry of Economic Affairs has flagged that a prior phase of this same conflict (April 2026) tripled the weekly oil import bill from roughly $300mn to $800mn, and PIDE has warned CPI could re-accelerate to 15-17% YoY under a severe, sustained disruption.

GCC states supply 55% of Pakistan's remittances (4.7% of GDP) — a prolonged Gulf slowdown tied to this conflict could squeeze that inflow channel just as the current account is trying to hold a surplus.

SBP's Jul 27 MPC decision is now a live event risk: petrol and diesel were already hiked Rs13.18/Rs13.80 per litre on Jul 11 and price reviews have moved to weekly — a further oil-driven inflation surprise could tilt the central bank hawkish.
